edbDesc: (capillarity, capillary motion, wicking) The movement of a liquid relative to a substance in contact. A result of the adhesive intermolecular forces between the liquid and the substance being stronger (or weaker) than the cohesive intermolecular forces inside the liquid. Causes a concave (or concave) meniscus to form where the liquid touches the surface. Can cause raising or lowering (e.g. mercury in glass) of the liquid.
title: Capillary Action
